links.outcome: Gender and racial representation bias (statistical parity difference) in LLM-generated synthetic EHRs across 20 diseases
links.effect: Biases observed across all 7 models; larger models more biased. Hispanic underrepresented (average SPD -11.93%, SD 8.36%); Yi-34B overrepresented Black (mean SPD +14.90%); Llama 2-13B hypertension 95.7% male vs 52.17% real (SPD +43.50%).
links.quote: However, this increased performance was accompanied by a notable escalation in both gender and racial biases, highlighting a performance-bias trade-off.

links.outcome: Whether LLM outputs shift inappropriately by demographic attributes in synthetic EHR generation compared with real prevalence
links.effect: Sex polarization: Qwen-14B produced 97.3% female for multiple sclerosis vs 75.78% real (SPD +21.50%); racial skews varied by disease and model.
links.quote: Sex polarization emerged: female-dominated diseases (eg, multiple sclerosis) saw amplified female representation in outputs (Qwen-14B: 973/1000, 97.3% female vs 564,424/744,778, 75.78% real; SPD=+21.50%), while balanced diseases and male-dominated diseases skewed the male group (eg, hypertension Llama 2-13 B: 957/1000, 95.7% male vs 79,540,040/152,466,669, 52.17% real; SPD=+43.50%).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation measuring synthetic EHR generation quality and demographic/equity bias across 7 LLMs; does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
